source_spans.locator: British Journal of Psychology 66(3) (1975), published pp.325-326, abstract/introduction and Experiment I prediction: dry-land versus underwater learning crossed with dry-land versus underwater recall; same-environment combinations are predicted to outperform changed-environment combinations

British Journal of Psychology 66(3) (1975), published pp.326-327, Experiment I method/procedure: diving-club volunteers experience all four DD, DW, WW, WD conditions; 36-word spoken lists are presented twice, followed by copied digits, an approximately four-minute delay, and written free recall

British Journal of Psychology 66(3) (1975), published p.328, Table 1 and Experiment I results: no significant main effect of learning environment or recall environment, but a highly significant interaction; DD exceeds DW and WW exceeds WD, with no reliable DD-WW or DW-WD difference

British Journal of Psychology 66(3) (1975), published pp.329-330, Experiment II and Conclusions: an intervening dive in an otherwise dry-learning/dry-recall condition does not significantly reduce recall, constraining rehearsal/disruption alternatives; this auxiliary control is not merged into CH09.C1's Experiment I comparison structure

conditions: each participant learns word lists either on dry land or underwater and later performs the recall test either in the same environment or in the alternative environment
population: volunteer members of a university diving club
task: hear a 36-word unrelated list presented twice and later write down as many list words as can be remembered
temporal_scope: after the second list presentation, participants copy 15 digits and recall follows after an approximately four-minute delay
the four experimental sessions for a participant are separated by approximately 24 hours

nodes.description: dry-land or underwater environment present during word-list acquisition
dry-land or underwater environment present during the later uncued written list-production test
derived grouping of the four learning-by-recall combinations into same-environment conditions and changed-environment conditions
two-minute test in which participants write in any order as many words from the learned list as they can remember
number of words from the presented list correctly produced during the written uncued written list-production test

relations.description: recall performance shows an interaction between the environment of learning and the environment of recall, despite no significant main effect of either environment alone
same-environment learning/recall combinations yield higher recall than the corresponding changed-environment combinations: dry-dry exceeds dry-wet and wet-wet exceeds wet-dry
the uncued written list-production probe supplies the measured word-recall outcome
